claims.text: A multiscale framework coupling ab initio treatment of local chemical ordering and lattice distortions to mesoscale phonon-transport simulations will predict phonon thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys more accurately than effective-medium models.
The proposed framework will be at least 30% more accurate than existing effective-medium models.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi can occur as a stable, single-phase FCC high-entropy alloy under the stated conditions.
The relevant operating temperature range is 300–500 K.
The target alloys have configurational entropy greater than 1.5 R.
Local lattice distortions enhance phonon scattering in high-entropy alloys.
Chemical short-range ordering enhances phonon scattering in high-entropy alloys.
Explicitly representing atomic-level disorder can translate local lattice distortions and short-range order into enhanced phonon scattering.
Enhanced phonon scattering caused by the represented disorder reduces the phonon mean free path.
Traditional effective-medium approximations average out local lattice-distortion and short-range-order effects.
Existing effective-medium models have approximately 15% error when predicting phonon thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys.
The proposed framework will reduce prediction error from approximately 15% to below 10% relative to experiment.
The framework will be robust only for high-entropy alloys with high configurational entropy.
Alloys below the configurational-entropy threshold may deviate from the model because of phase separation or anisotropic microstructures.
The approach is applicable exclusively to stable, single-phase high-entropy alloys with configurational entropy greater than 1.5 R.
Phase separation, anisotropic microstructures, or lower configurational entropy will diminish the utility of the approach.
Time-domain thermoreflectance can provide the experimental thermal-conductivity benchmark used to assess the predictions.
Prediction error greater than 10% for in-domain, single-phase, high-configurational-entropy alloys would falsify the anticipated accuracy improvement.

contradictions.description: The applicability boundary excludes alloys at or below 1.5 R and other out-of-domain states, but the experiment varies configurational entropy and the first clause of the falsification rule refers broadly to high-entropy alloys. As written, poor results for an out-of-domain sample could falsify a hypothesis that simultaneously declares that sample outside its scope.
